At ten in the evening, a plane with a specialized black paint coating passed over the palace at Velnaz. The bay doors opened, and from them jumped a single person: Cecilia Hiacynt, dressed with black clothes covering her inner clothing, specialized tactical earmuffs covering her elven ears, and a black military cloth covering her lower face. There was a parachute pack on her back.

She jumped. Pulling the cord at the opportune moment, the parachute rapidly opened like a flower in full bloom, slowing her descent, and she landed in front of the large doors of the palace. She quickly collected the parachute cloth together, bundling it into her hands, before knocking on the palace door.

[quote=corzerran;61402514]She walked, undisturbed by the lack of conversation, through the path assigned to her by her superiors. It did seem odd, but she was accustomed to moving through the world on her own.

Agnieszka nodded and stepped into the elevator, going up high to the floor she had been indicated. Now she was alone with the sound of humming machines, their presence simultaneously overbearing and a comforting white noise. It reminded her of the resonance beneath the lower sanctum of the Nexite Church in Solaria, where the bones of saints lay in perfect peace and the fountains of affliction had run dry. Only that this was different, it was nothing like the holy pursuit of knowledge she had dedicated her life to. If it were up to her, it would be called-

Her thoughts were interrupted by the ding of the elevator. The doors slid open, and she stepped out.[/quote]
The humming seemed quieter, but different here. More deliberate. As her robes flowed through the breezeless halls of the most high office, she would see a spartan grey paint job adorning the metallic walls. This was until she reached the turn to the left, and saw the office of [b][u]Him[/u][/b], the Overseer Superior, Li Jinping, in the flesh. Well, mostly flesh, his robotic arm was plain for all to see.  The floor was carpeted in red. In the back centre of the room, a Black Walnut desk sat in the surprisingly mostly empty room facing away from the large overlooking window, a modern computer sat on the edge of the desk, facing away from the Keeper. The room was large, though it could be considered devoid of any life and decoration, except that to her right was a large portrait of his wife, Ou Tangliang. To her left, a gigantic screen mounted the entire wall, though it remained inactive.
